title: Independent stance-leg force
effort: Produce upward and short forward force from each stance leg while controlling the pelvis and receiving on two feet.
quality_marker: In E1 record each takeoff leg, actual hand/arm strategy and whether the two-foot reception is quiet and held for 2 s. An uncontrolled first attempt triggers the grounded replacement for remaining attempts; no extra prerequisite test or symmetry claim is added. Use the listed attempts only; a miss or invalid attempt consumes the dose. Record actual attempts, setup and any substitutions; no bonus tests or comparison across unlike tasks.
brief: Six low, isolated one-leg vertical takeoffs anchor the session. Grounded lead-biased hip initiation, supported one-leg knee force, ankle force and hip finish support them; two short forward takeoffs provide a small vector transfer. No same-leg landing series is prescribed.

explosive.name: Single-Leg Vertical Takeoff — two-foot floor reception
explosive.key: Single-Leg Vertical Takeoff — two-foot floor reception
explosive.job: Main independent stance-leg upward push with a deliberately broader receiving base.
explosive.cue: Stand on one leg, make a small controlled dip and project a modest height; bring both feet under the pelvis and receive on two feet, holding 2 s. Three attempts per takeoff leg. No extra preparatory hop.
explosive.replacement: two bouts of three bilateral settled-start squat jumps with hands at hips, 10 s between reps and 60 s between bouts, then the same 90 s transition; hold the start 2 s without a second dip and receive on both feet for 2 s. This replaces unilateral takeoffs with bilateral takeoffs and differs from E3 grounded single-leg force. If bilateral receiving also fails, stop the remaining flight work and record a modified session
explosive.identity: Proposed floor-reception execution; single-leg-takeoff-to-two-foot-box-landing is a related verified parent, not an exact match
explosive.novelty_reason: Isolates the takeoff leg while keeping bilateral receiving, unlike Week 3 two-foot split-stance takeoff. Repeated same-leg hops would add an unnecessary receiving demand.
explosive.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 60 s, then the other leg; 6 total reps; 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Kettlebell Swing — staggered dead-stop repetitions
explosive.job: Start hip-driven force from a parked bell with a lead-biased but two-foot base.
explosive.cue: Use a shallow stagger and very light bell, hips/pelvis square. Hike, drive one chest-height float and park; reset before the next rep. Complete two per lead leg, without arm lifting or twisting.
explosive.replacement: a supported single-leg rapid hinge return at the same per-leg dose, with no bell, if parking control or minimum bell load is unsuitable
explosive.identity: kettlebell-swing family; staggered parked execution proposed
explosive.novelty_reason: Removes the continuous return of Week 5 while retaining lead-biased hip initiation. This constraint serves force from rest, not a claim of a new swing family.
explosive.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 45 s, then the other leg; 4 total reps; 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Single-Leg Squat Rise — supported rapid quarter-range
explosive.key: Single-Leg Squat Rise — supported rapid quarter-range
explosive.job: Express stance-leg knee extension without flight or a rear foot contributing.
explosive.cue: Hold stable support, free foot clear; lower to a shallow controlled squat for 2 s, hold 1 s and rise quickly through the whole foot. Use the hand for balance/needed assistance, not a sudden pull.
explosive.replacement: a supported split-squat rapid rise at the same per-leg dose when the single-leg position cannot stay organized
explosive.identity: Proposed supported single-leg rapid squat execution
explosive.novelty_reason: Removes rear-leg contribution from the earlier split squat while avoiding another landing dose. A deep single-leg squat was rejected as needless range/skill demand.
explosive.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 45 s, then the other leg; 4 total reps; 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Bent-Knee Calf Raise — single-leg rapid supported rise
explosive.key: Bent-Knee Calf Raise — single-leg rapid supported rise
explosive.job: Produce quick stance-ankle force while holding a modest knee bend.
explosive.cue: Use stable hand support, keep one foot on the floor and knee softly bent; rise quickly onto the forefoot, hold 1 s and lower 2 s. Forefoot stays grounded.
explosive.replacement: an assisted bilateral bent-knee rapid raise for the same set/rep count if needed; record changed laterality
explosive.identity: bent-knee-soleus-raise family; unilateral rapid execution proposed
explosive.novelty_reason: Retain the six familiar flexed-knee single-ankle rapid reps while takeoff laterality changes. A new pogo variant would add contacts without improving this isolated ankle job.
explosive.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 45 s, then the other leg; 6 total reps; 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Glute Bridge — single-leg rapid rise with level pelvis
explosive.key: Glute Bridge — single-leg rapid rise with level pelvis
explosive.job: Express hip extension on each side without the second leg hiding pelvic control.
explosive.cue: One foot grounded, other thigh comfortably lifted; drive hips up quickly, hold 1 s, lower 2 s without twist. Use bodyweight and a short controllable range.
explosive.replacement: a kickstand-assisted rapid bridge at the same per-leg dose if the pelvis rotates; record assistance
explosive.identity: bodyweight-glute-bridge parent; unilateral rapid execution proposed
explosive.novelty_reason: Retain four familiar single-leg floor-bridge outputs to express near-finish hip force without a lengthened hinge or landing. A new elevated-foot bridge is unnecessary equipment and leverage change.
explosive.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 45 s, then the other leg; 4 total reps; 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Single-Leg Forward Takeoff — two-foot floor reception
explosive.key: Single-Leg Forward Takeoff — two-foot floor reception
explosive.job: Apply the independent leg push to a short forward rather than upward projection.
explosive.cue: One modest forward takeoff per leg from a quiet single-leg stance; use a small dip, project into the marked receiving zone and bring both feet to a controlled 2 s reception. No distance target or extra hop.
explosive.replacement: one supported fast step-up per leg without flight, using the same 60 s side recovery, if a forward reception cannot fit or stay controlled
explosive.identity: Proposed single-leg forward takeoff to bilateral floor reception
explosive.novelty_reason: Changes the force vector from E1 with only two exploratory attempts. A long unilateral bound series would need more receiving capacity and space than this job requires.
explosive.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 60 s, then the other leg; 2 total reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

resilience.name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction — light
resilience.job: Light lateral-hip strengthening to keep the pelvis and knee organized over the force-producing leg.
resilience.cue: Lie on side, lower leg bent; lift upper leg slightly 2 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s with toes facing forward and pelvis still. Bodyweight is sufficient unless clearly easy.
resilience.replacement: a smaller unloaded leg lift with the same per-leg dose
resilience.identity: Proposed exact execution; no verified canonical ID
resilience.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 30 s, then the other leg; 10 total reps; 45 s before the next exercise/section

resilience.name: Seated Band Ankle Inversion — light
resilience.job: Light inner-ankle strengthening to organize the foot arch without toe clawing.
resilience.cue: Heel supported; hand-held light band draws the forefoot outward. Move forefoot inward 2 s, hold 1 s, return 2 s with shin still.
resilience.replacement: gentle hand resistance through a smaller range at the same per-leg dose
resilience.identity: Proposed exact dynamic execution; no exact canonical ID

primary.cue: Lower 3 s, rise in about 1 s without changing stance width; front whole foot stays loaded and pelvis stays square.
primary.replacement: a supported split squat with lighter load or bodyweight at a challenging controlled depth

primary.name: Hamstring Walkout — complete out-and-back cycle
primary.job: Knee-flexor leverage while the pelvis stays raised, distinct from moving through a hip hinge.
primary.cue: Start in a bilateral bridge. Each cycle is two small heel steps out per foot, then two back per foot: eight placements in about 8 s. Keep a soft knee and level hips; never chase a fully straight leg.
primary.replacement: a shorter-lever walkout at the same complete-cycle count; reduce range for sagging or cramp and stop if control does not return

E: Use light resistance or bodyweight that permits visibly rapid force with control. Begin with E1 while fresh. Each row has a distinct job; supporting work stays small. Rest may be extended to 2–3 minutes when speed, control or attention has not returned. Stop for pain, loss of alignment, stiff/asymmetric landing or clear slowing; rest and regress remaining work only if control returns, otherwise record stopped work. Never make up failed attempts. No drop landings or rotational throws are prescribed.
S: Light controlled strengthening, at least 5 technical reps in reserve. Do not chase burn, shaking or pre-fatigue. Reduce load/range when control fades; stop for symptoms.
P: Working sets are challenging at about 2–3 technical reps/cycles in reserve. Select load/lever from demonstrated ability, not age or calendar week. Keep the stated controlled lowering and complete range; no forced repetitions, maximum testing or conditioning circuit. Check late-set and late-session quality; record reductions instead of forcing nominal completion.

setup: Keep both receiving tasks in the marked short-takeoff area, leaving the rest of the lane clear. No box reception or running approach is required. Stable hand supports must be independently inspected. The single-leg calf preparation and work are separately dosed per leg. Inspect stable supports, minimum loads, surface grip and all active/waiting/return paths. Keep one athlete active per lane under suitable supervision; no group size or station count is assumed. Three separate 10 m lanes are not a 30 m runway. Ball releases need separately verified flight/bounce/roll containment. Replacements occupy the original slot; missing readiness or equipment can change the practice exposure and actual totals. Before applying multiple replacements, check the other rows: a replacement must not duplicate an exercise already delivered in another slot. Do not add duplicate work just to fill the count. If the supplied replacements cannot preserve distinct jobs, stop the affected slot and record a modified/incomplete session for revision; do not claim the planned six distinct explosive tasks were completed. Changed reset time, takeoff/landing type, sides and reps belong in the actual record.
delivery: Estimate 58–65 minutes after Access & Prepare 1 for an athlete with equipment access. Includes work, resets, listed recovery, preparation, transitions and 10–16 minutes of extra instruction/setup; additional queues, rest or load-finding add time. Existing preparation duration and total booking fit remain unresolved. Never compress needed recovery to fit a clock. One coached focus class per week for twelve weeks. Review actual sport, leg lifting, running, jumping and tumbling before delivery. Initially allow roughly 48–72 hours before another demanding leg exposure when the full schedule permits, adjusting to actual recovery; a week elapsed is not proof of readiness. Resume missed classes without doubling up. No additional full workouts or body-control blocks are prescribed.
progression: Week 6 deliberately reduced work. This conditional week restores eight landing events with eight single-leg takeoffs, six primary rounds/eight bouts and 34 conventional reps plus two walkout cycles. Split Squat returns at 1 × 4 per leg; RDL/bridge become 1 × 5; supported Single-Leg Calf Raise 1 × 5 per leg replaces bilateral straight-knee calf loading. Goblet Squat is omitted because lead-leg knee force is the priority. Do not restore this demand merely because the midpoint week was authored: hold Week 6 or use the listed lower-complexity replacements if actual readiness is unconfirmed at delivery.
audit_findings: Eight takeoffs are unilateral but all eight landings are bilateral; the two counts describe different demands. The two forward attempts are a vector transfer, not a distance test. Two exact supporting repeats protect clarity while four changed executions have declared jobs. Side-specific strength bouts rise from six to eight despite six rounds; individual load selection and preparation account for the new supported single-leg calf task.
